note: Pacing for the runner (scripts/pacing.py, D-486). The two budgets are PLACEHOLDERS: the plan's real limits are not published as token counts and Casey has not read them yet. They are in weighted tokens (see weights), sized from K9's measured tasks (a Sonnet worker plus an Opus review is about 0.5M to 1M weighted tokens). Replace them with measured figures once a usage limit has been hit and its reset recorded in state.usage.limit_hit, or once a quota command (PACING_QUOTA_CMD) reports utilisation, which then wins over this ledger. The runner sets PACING_QUOTA_CMD to quota_cmd_default when the variable is unset; scripts/quota_probe.py reads the session's own plan usage and is verified at the D-486 rehearsal (D-486). Calibration October 31, 2026 (D-1110): Casey read about 50% of the weekly plan used while this ledger stood at 102M weighted tokens (window from 2026-10-29T18:38Z, reset Thursday 2026-11-05T18:38Z), so the weekly budget is 200M until the quota probe (state.usage.source is still "ledger": the probe falls back silently) or a recorded limit_hit gives a better figure; the five-hour budget stays as it was for want of a reading. Spend line (D-1128, October 31): Casey wants the week's budget used up by Thursday morning, not run out early and then idle, so `spread` holds the week's spend to a straight line from the anchor reading (the ledger at 23:30Z, October 31) to the effective budget three hours before the reset; remove `spread` to return to claim-when-it-fits. Re-anchored November 1 (D-1167): the first in-band reading (D-1155) at 01:02Z said 59% of the week used, so the line now starts at 118M of the 200M week (plan units, the same unit the reading gives the pacer) and `headroom` drops from 0.1 to 0.03 so the line ends near 97% three hours before the reset the reading reports (2026-11-05T17:00Z), as Casey asked: no tokens left over on Thursday morning; the ledger, used only when no reading is under six hours old, sits about 10% below the plan and so under-claims for a while, never over.

actions_minutes.note: GitHub Actions quota read by Claude from Casey's billing page in his browser on October 29, 2026 (D-494): GitHub Pro includes 3,000 Linux minutes a month on a private repository, reset on the 1st; October's use to the 29th was about 430 minutes (gross $3.44 at $0.008 a minute, billed $0). The runner keeps the month's projected use under the included figure less headroom; with the Rust Ci at the 15-minute warm ceiling plus Twin, Ally and Governance (about 2 minutes together) and a push and a pull-request run per task, a cycle costs at most about 35 minutes, so the month allows about 80 cycles at the ceiling and more as Ci's cache warms.
